findings.title: Public findMany API is removed without migrating any callers
findings.body: This change replaces the service's public findMany(findManyArgs) method with getBaseConditions() and only updates this service and its integration test. Any existing caller that invoked InsightsBookingService.findMany to fetch BookingTimeStatusDenormalized rows will now fail TypeScript compilation/runtime, and no caller in this PR is migrated to construct a $queryRaw query with the returned conditions. Either keep a compatible findMany implemented on top of the raw conditions or update/search for all callers in the same change.

findings.title: Authorization fragments return unparenthesized top-level OR conditions
findings.body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition (and the team equivalent at line 196-207) returns SQL of the form `(team condition) OR (user condition)` with no outer parentheses, and getFilterConditions likewise returns an unparenthesized `(eventTypeId = ...) OR (eventParentId = ...)` for a single filter. These are public composable fragments; if a caller embeds them as `WHERE ${conditions} AND <date/status predicates>` instead of going through getBaseConditions, SQL AND binds tighter than OR, so the second OR branch escapes the preceding predicates and can return bookings outside the intended date/status/auth-filter window. Wrap each composite condition in outer parentheses at construction so the fragments are safe to compose anywhere.

findings.title: Org/team ANY(array) raw SQL is never actually executed against the database
findings.body: The org and team authorization tests only assert structural equality of Prisma.sql objects (strings/values); the sole test that executes SQL (line 481) uses user scope, whose condition contains no ANY(array) parameter and no OR branch. Whether Prisma/Postgres binds a JavaScript number[] supplied as `= ANY(${teamIds})` / `= ANY(${userIds})` correctly is therefore unverified, even though org/team insights depend entirely on that binding. Extend the $queryRaw integration test to org and team scopes (and to an OR filter combination) so a binding or precedence failure fails the suite instead of shipping silently.

findings.title: Caching behavior tests were deleted while the service still caches conditions
findings.body: The PR removes the entire 'Caching' describe block, but InsightsBookingService still keeps cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions and short-circuits on them (insightsBooking.ts lines 49-50, 83-95). There is now no test that a second call returns the cached Prisma.Sql or that repeated calls do not rebuild/re-query memberships, so a regression in the caching fields (e.g. caching the shared NOTHING_CONDITION result incorrectly across calls) would go undetected. Restore the caching tests adapted to Prisma.sql expectations.
